Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we prep the internal decision packet: can you provide a concise Private vs Dedicated sizing recommendation for our pilot (10k monthly active endpoints, bursty daytime traffic, strict PHI isolation requirements)? Specifically we need:

- Estimated GPU count and class (e.g., 8x A100/80GB equiv) for both hosting modes
- Expected average and p95 latency assumptions under our workload
- Cost delta (monthly) and any minimum commitment implications
- Any operational caveats (onboarding time, network/VPC requirements, audit evidence you will supply)

Procurement will want a draft SOW and a high-level cost model to include in the package. Can you reply by early next week?

Thanks,

Subject: Segregated fleet — sizing options (attached)

Team / Sara — attached is a concise worksheet (isolation-cost-model.xlsx) and my notes below. High level assumptions: 10k MAU mapped to ~60 QPS peak (regionally concentrated), tokenization workload is mixed (short prompts 12–28 tokens, responses avg 120 tokens). We assume model family equivalent to redwood-2-small for chat workloads; if Medicorp requires larger models we'll need to re-run.

Option A — Dedicated (Redwood hosted, tenant-dedicated pool)
- Recommended baseline: 8x H100-80GB (or equivalent) for pilot; supports sustained 60 QPS with average latency 120–180ms and p95 ~420ms with continuous batching and KV-prefix caching.
- Autoscale buffer: +2 GPUs for burst (policy-controlled).
- Cost: ~$62k/month (compute + reserved capacity amortized) — see tab "Dedicated-pilot" in workbook. Minimum commitment: 3 months recommended; contract-level SLA available.
- Pros: faster onboarding (~2 weeks), no customer infra changes, Redwood handles backups and patching.
- Cons: Logical isolation; you’ll get tenant-level encryption, but hardware isolation requires Private.

Option B — Private (VPC / customer-managed network or on-prem air-gapped bundle)
- Recommended baseline: 10x H100-80GB (to account for telemetry/ops redundancy and stricter network segmentation); expected avg latency 110–160ms but p95 slightly higher under tight node failure (~450–500ms) before rebalancing.
- Ops overhead: initial provisioning ~4–6 weeks (longer if on-prem hardware procurement).
- Cost: higher upfront (hardware + provisioning) — equivalent monthly run-rate estimate ~$88k/month when amortized over 36 months (sheet "Private-pilot"). Procurement implications: hardware purchase order or 12–36 month platform license.
- Pros: physical isolation, customer-managed keys (HSM), full on-prem auditability.
- Cons: longer lead time, additional ops from Medicorp side unless managed package purchased.

Security / evidence: we will provide SOC2 Type II summary, encryption-at-rest docs, architecture diagram for VPC peering, and sample audit log extracts. For Private on-prem we’ll produce airgap verification checklist and HSM integration guide.

Attachments referenced: isolation-cost-model.xlsx (spreadsheet with line-item monthly TCO and capacity curves).

—Karthik
Principal Deal Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Segregated fleet — sizing & next steps

Sara / Procurement — following Karthik’s recommendations, attached is a one-page summary and the draft SOW (medicorp-sow-draft.pdf) for your review. Key asks from Procurement to move to contracting:

1) Confirm hosting posture preference (Dedicated hosted pool vs Private VPC / On-prem).
2) If Dedicated: confirm minimum term (we recommend 3 months pilot commit).
3) If Private: confirm whether Medicorp will provision hardware or if you want our managed on-prem bundle (we can include turnkey procurement as a line item).

Proposed timeline assuming Dedicated decision:
- Tue Jun 26: Finalize SOW and cost table
- Wed Jun 27: Legal review / redlines begin
- Mon Jul 1: Pilot kickoff (environment provisioned)

If you decide Private, add 4–6 weeks prep for procurement/provisioning.

Attachments: medicorp-sow-draft.pdf (draft SOW), isolation-cost-model.xlsx (line-item workbook).

—Marissa

If anyone on our side has risks to flag for this approach, call them out now — otherwise I’ll push the MAP and updated SOW to the HubSpot deal and DocuSign link this afternoon.
